title: Keep interlocking declaration, runtime, Station Master and trace bilaterally bound (Bun)

facts.note: The surfaces the detector walks: interlocking YAML route space, train artifacts, Station Master JOURNEY_MAP, InterlockingRunner runtime, e2e trace tests. Presence of either the route space or an InterlockingRunner makes the tree an interlocking system.
Bun-stack rendering only; other stacks own their own packages.

values: interlocking route/entrypoint declared, edited or removed
train artifact added, renamed or deleted
InterlockingRunner resolution or TrainRunner delegation edited
trace emission added, edited or removed
JOURNEY_MAP interlocking mapping added, edited or removed
reachability field added to interlocking YAML
facts.note: Diff-level facts; needs an observer that classifies the edit by binding surface. Not edit-only: existing violations are covered by the finding fact.
Detector findings on the whole consumer tree (including pre-existing violations in unchanged files) must be surfaced to the activation layer with the failing direction.

fires: A Bun consumer repo has (or gains) a declared interlocking route whose train artifact does not exist, e.g. a route added or a train artifact deleted/renamed.
InterlockingRunner code returns a routeId/selectedTrainId literal not declared in any interlocking YAML.
A JOURNEY_MAP interlocking mapping points at a path with no YAML or an undeclared interlockingId.
An interlocking marked entrypoint.exposed=true has none of its entrypoint.actions wired in JOURNEY_MAP.
An executed interlocking route emits no trace metadata, or emits trace interlockingId/routeId values that do not resolve to the declared YAML.
An e2e trace test asserts a trace.routeId/interlockingId absent from the declared route space.
An interlocking YAML gains a field such as `reachability` or `station_actions` instead of core `entrypoint`.
The detector reports an existing binding violation in a tree the task did not otherwise touch on that surface.
A repo has an InterlockingRunner but no interlocking route space (or vice versa).
doesNotFire: A consumer tree with neither an interlocking route space nor an InterlockingRunner.
An interlocking with entrypoint.exposed:false lacking a JOURNEY_MAP action (only the declaration_to_station direction is exempt).
A non-Bun stack rendering of interlocking (owned by its own workspace package).

given: A Bun consumer repo with an interlocking route space (plan/_trains/_interlockings/**) or an InterlockingRunner
when: you add, change or delete any binding surface (interlocking YAML, train artifact, runtime resolver/delegation, JOURNEY_MAP, trace emission or e2e trace test), or the detector reports a binding violation
then: Keep all five directions closed: every declared route resolves through InterlockingRunner to its declared trainId (train artifact exists); the runtime resolves only declared routeIds/trainIds before TrainRunner delegation; every JOURNEY_MAP mapping points at an existing declared interlocking; every entrypoint.exposed=true interlocking is reachable via one of its entrypoint.actions; every executed route emits trace metadata whose interlockingId/routeId resolve to the declared YAML.
prefer: Close the direction named in the violation: add the missing train artifact; remove or declare a hidden routeId/trainId literal; repoint the JOURNEY_MAP path at the real YAML; wire the exposed interlocking's entrypoint.action into JOURNEY_MAP; assert only declared trace interlockingId/routeId values.
If an interlocking is genuinely internal, set entrypoint.exposed:false with a reason instead of wiring it.
Read core `entrypoint.exposed`/`entrypoint.actions` as owned by core; follow core if its name or shape changes.

Follow the additive call chain (core runtime spec #1251): interlocking YAML -> entrypoint.actions[] -> JOURNEY_MAP action -> InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain(...) -> InterlockingResolution(routeId, trainId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...) -> TrainRunner.execute(selectedTrainId) -> trace(interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, ...), so the validator can resolve the trace back to the YAML route.
avoid: Hidden routes: runtime routeId/selectedTrainId literals declared in no interlocking YAML.
Parallel reachability fields (`entrypoints`, `runtime_exposure`, `station_actions`, `exposed_actions`, `reachability`) that fork core `entrypoint` — schema drift; replace them with core `entrypoint`.
Dangling JOURNEY_MAP mappings, executed routes without trace emission, or trace assertions on undeclared values.
unless: Interlockings with entrypoint.exposed:false (internal-transition-only / library-only / planned-not-exposed) carry no Station-Master-reachability (declaration_to_station) obligation.
A tree with no interlocking route space and no InterlockingRunner is not an interlocking system; the rule does not bite.
why: Bilateral binding is what makes interlocking a route-control system rather than a description; any broken direction lets declaration, runtime, Station Master and trace drift apart silently, so it blocks CI.
evidence: bun_interlocking_binding reports no violation for any of the five directions or schema drift on the consumer tree.
Each violation names its failing `direction` in evidence; the fix closes that direction.

Detector fails on fixtures/dirty (declaration_to_runtime), fixtures/dirty_runtime_hidden (runtime_to_declaration), fixtures/dirty_station_missing (station_to_declaration), fixtures/dirty_unreachable (declaration_to_station), fixtures/dirty_trace (trace_to_declaration) and passes the clean tree.
verifier_detail: One JS detector `bun_interlocking_binding` walks plan/_trains/_interlockings/** (route space), server.ts (Station Master JOURNEY_MAP), src/trains/** (InterlockingRunner runtime) and e2e/** (trace tests), emitting RAW v1.1 violations under this single rule_id with the failing `direction` in evidence, plus a schema-drift signal when a parallel reachability field is used instead of core #1248 `entrypoint`.

declaration_to_runtime: every declared route resolves through InterlockingRunner to the declared trainId — the route's train artifact (train_path / plan/_trains/<train_id>.yaml) must exist so the runtime can load it. Fail fixture: fixtures/dirty.

runtime_to_declaration: InterlockingRunner never resolves a routeId/trainId absent from the loaded YAML; a runtime returning a routeId/selectedTrainId literal not declared in any interlocking is a hidden route. Fail fixture: fixtures/dirty_runtime_hidden.

station_to_declaration: every Station Master interlocking mapping ({interlockingId, path}) points to an existing interlocking YAML; a mapping whose path resolves to no file or names an undeclared interlockingId is a dangling route. Fail fixture: fixtures/dirty_station_missing.

declaration_to_station: every interlocking with core entrypoint.exposed=true is Station-Master-reachable through one of its core entrypoint.actions wired into JOURNEY_MAP to that interlocking. Consumes core afokapu/atdd#1248 entrypoint.exposed + entrypoint.actions; defines no parallel reachability field. Fail fixture: fixtures/dirty_unreachable.

trace_to_declaration: every executed interlocking route emits trace metadata resolving back to the source YAML; a trace test asserting trace.routeId / trace.interlockingId values absent from the declared route space does not bind the run to its declaration (core afokapu/atdd#1251 trace contract). Fail fixture: fixtures/dirty_trace.

Call model whose closure is enforced (core runtime spec afokapu/atdd#1251, additive): plan/_trains/_interlockings/<id>.yaml (declaration, core #1248) -> entrypoint.actions[] (core #1248 entrypoint field, CONSUMED here) -> Station Master JOURNEY_MAP action (reachability, server.ts) -> InterlockingRunner.resolveTrain(...) (runtime, core #1251) -> InterlockingResolution(routeId, trainId, category, guardId, resolutionStrategy, ...) -> TrainRunner.execute(selectedTrainId) (delegation) -> trace(interlockingId, routeId, selectedTrainId, ...) -> validator resolves the trace back to the YAML route.

Ownership split (collision prevention): core afokapu/atdd#1248/#1249 own the interlocking YAML schema and the shape/allowed values of `entrypoint`; this extension only READS those core fields to validate reachability against Station Master and runtime traces in a consumer repo. It MUST NOT introduce `entrypoints`, `runtime_exposure`, `station_actions`, `exposed_actions`, `reachability` or any other parallel reachability field. If core #1248 changes the field name or shape, this rule follows core and updates its detector/fixtures.

Term parallel_reachability_field: any non-core reachability field (entrypoints, runtime_exposure, station_actions, exposed_actions, reachability) that forks core afokapu/atdd#1248's `entrypoint`; using one is schema drift.
Term hidden_route: a routeId/selectedTrainId the InterlockingRunner runtime resolves that is declared in no interlocking YAML — a runtime-to-declaration binding break.

Term bilateral_binding: the property that interlocking declaration, runtime resolution, Station Master reachability and execution trace are bound in both directions so none can drift from the others undetected.
The detector emits RAW facts only; the strict verdict is applied by a downstream gate.
Scope: Bun stack only; per-stack renderings other than Bun are owned by their own workspace packages.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

severity 1, disposition strict. Disposition justification: a broken binding direction — unresolvable declared route, hidden runtime route, dangling Station Master mapping, unreachable exposed interlocking, or a trace not resolving to its declaration — is the exact silent-drift failure class the train-interlocking design (afokapu/atdd#1246) exists to close; it therefore blocks CI.
Bun-stack realization of the agnostic core obligation `coder.train.interlocking-bilateral-binding`; rendered for the Bun backend.
Per boundary spec §6.2 the core contracts are referenced NARRATIVELY, and the core `entrypoint` field is CONSUMED, never forked.

Closure surfaces: declaration (interlocking YAML route space, core #1248), runtime resolution (InterlockingRunner, core #1251), Station Master reachability (server.ts JOURNEY_MAP), TrainRunner delegation, execution trace.

splitSuggestion.then: Express interlocking reachability only through core `entrypoint.exposed`/`entrypoint.actions`; never add a parallel reachability field.

sharedNodes.text: strict: a finding is not advisory; a strict finding blocks CI.

additions.text: The schema-drift obligation (no parallel reachability field; consume core `entrypoint`) is independent of the five-direction closure and could be its own convention; kept here in avoid/prefer/verifier_detail since the source detector emits it under this rule_id.

The five directions are merged into one closure obligation; coder-facing text (~2,000 chars) exceeds the ~1,000-character guideline because the five directions, both exceptions and the runtime call chain (InterlockingResolution fields, TrainRunner.execute(selectedTrainId), trace payload) must be visible to the coder.
additions.justification: Lossless placement wins over brevity; auditor required the runtime call chain and trace emission to be coder-facing.
